findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same index
findings.body:
`BuildIndex` used to hold `cacheMu` for its whole body, which serialized index builds. Now the lock is only taken around the final cache assignment. `getOrCreateIndex` does an unlocked check-then-build (`GetIndex` returns nil, then `build`). Search requests and watch events (`handleEvent`) can therefore build the same NamespacedResource at the same time.

Consequences:
- For file-backed indexes, two `bleve.New` calls race on the same directory, and one fails or corrupts the other.
- For memory indexes, the last writer silently replaces the cached index. Watch-event writes that went to the discarded instance are lost.
- `IndexTenants` and `IndexedKinds` metrics are double-counted.

The lock needs to become per-key (e.g., singleflight or a per-key mutex), not just narrower.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`. Builds triggered by Search requests or watch events can write to the map at the same moment (line 138). This is a concurrent map read/write, which can crash the process with a fatal `concurrent map iteration and map write`. `TotalDocs` should take `RLock`.

findings.title: Stop no longer prevents further requests from being served
findings.body: Every handler used to call `s.Init(ctx)`. After `Stop` set `s.initErr` to "service is stopping" or "service is stopped", those calls returned that error and new requests were rejected. With the `Init` calls removed, nothing reads `initErr` anymore. After `Stop`, requests now go straight to a stopped backend whose lifecycle and poller have been cancelled. The result is undefined errors or hangs instead of a clean "service is stopped" error. Either add an explicit stopped check to the handlers or drop the now-dead `initErr` bookkeeping in `Stop`.

findings.title: Constructor now blocks on full index build and fails hard on any index error
findings.body:
`NewResourceServer` now runs lifecycle init and builds every search index synchronously, with no timeout, before returning. Any indexing error for a single namespace or resource (e.g., a document builder failure) now prevents the whole storage server from being constructed. Previously such an error only affected requests.

It also means every caller and test that constructs a server pays the full indexing cost at construction time. The description explicitly asks what lazy init callers might break, and this failure-mode change is not handled or tested.

findings.title: Data race on shared err and counter in parallel init workers
findings.body: Each errgroup goroutine assigns the outer `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments `totalBatchesIndexed` without synchronization. The PR's goal is to raise effective build concurrency, which makes these races more likely to occur. As a result, the reported `namespaced_indexed` count is wrong and the race detector will flag this code. Use a local `err :=` and an `atomic.Int64` counter.

findings.title: Integration test disabled for postgres instead of being fixed
findings.body: The storage-server integration test is now skipped for postgres, in addition to the existing sqlite skip. This probably masks a regression from moving initialization into the constructor: the server now blocks on init before the metrics endpoint comes up within the 500ms sleep. Postgres coverage of the startup path is lost exactly when startup behavior changes.
